questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Cameroon?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Cameroon article.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Cameroon?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Cameroon article.

questions.proof: French and English are the official languages.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The German Empire ruled Cameroon from _____ until World War I when France took the majority and Britain took the northwest and southwest.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the nineteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Cameroon article.

questions.proof: The German Empire ruled Cameroon from 1884 until World War I when France took the majority and Britain took the northwest and southwest.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “On 12 November _____, the President changed the divisions from provinces to regions.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Regions” part of the Cameroon article.

questions.proof: On 12 November 2008, the President changed the divisions from provinces to regions.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The country's neighbours are _____ to the west; Chad to the northeast; the Central African Republic to the east; and Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, and the Republic of the Congo to the south.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “neighbours”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Cameroon article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: The country's neighbours are Nigeria to the west; Chad to the northeast; the Central African Republic to the east; and Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, and the Republic of the Congo to the south.
